lesson.subject: data-ai
lesson.title: Computers, Data & AI Check-In: Where Am I?
lesson.summary: A friendly tour of instructions, sorting, graphs, smart machines and staying safe online, so we can see what you already know.
learning_objectives: Show what I know about instructions and patterns
Show what I know about sorting and simple graphs
Show what I know about smart machines and staying safe

blocks.markdown:
Computers follow **instructions** exactly, one step at a time.

A list of clear steps is called an **algorithm**.

Today is a **check-in** to see what you know. No computer is needed!

blocks.alt: Beep boop! Robots follow instructions one step at a time.
blocks.caption: Beep boop! Robots follow instructions one step at a time.

blocks.markdown:
If you give a robot the steps for a sandwich in the wrong order, you get a very silly sandwich!

The **order** of the steps matters.

blocks.title: A sandwich in the right order

scenes.caption: First, put the bread on the plate.
Last, put the top bread on. Yum!

question.prompt: Put these steps for brushing teeth in order.

blocks.markdown:
Computers love **patterns**. A pattern repeats in the same order.

We can also **sort** things into groups, such as animals that fly and animals that swim.

blocks.alt: A pattern: circle, triangle, circle, triangle ...
blocks.caption: A pattern: circle, triangle, circle, triangle ...

scenes.caption: Birds fly. Fish swim. Let us sort them.

question.prompt: Which one belongs in the group of fruits?

blocks.title: Be the robot
materials: A small toy or a cushion
instructions: Ask the grown-up to give you instructions: step forward, turn left, pick up the toy.
Do only what they say, one step at a time.
Now swap! Can you give clear instructions?

blocks.markdown:
**Data** is information we collect. We can count things with tally marks.

We can draw a **pictogram** where each picture stands for one item.

blocks.title: Tally marks: favourite pets
blocks.caption: Each stroke is one vote. Five is a bundle.

blocks.title: A pictogram: fruit we like
blocks.caption: Each picture is one child's vote. Bananas have the most.

question.prompt: A pictogram shows 3 🍎 for apples and 5 🍌 for bananas. Which fruit is more popular?

blocks.markdown:
An **input** is how we tell a computer something, like a keyboard or a touch screen.

An **output** is how it tells us something, like a screen or a speaker.

A **bug** is a mistake in the instructions. **Debugging** means fixing it.

blocks.alt: A keyboard and mouse are inputs. A screen and speaker are outputs.
blocks.caption: A keyboard and mouse are inputs. A screen and speaker are outputs.

question.prompt: A robot must go forward 2 steps and then turn left. It turned left first. What is the problem?

options.text: The steps are in the wrong order

blocks.text: Stop 5: Smart machines and staying safe

blocks.markdown:
Some machines can learn from examples. They are called **AI**, short for **artificial intelligence**.

A phone that understands your voice uses AI. But computers do not think or feel like people.

Online, keep your **password** secret. Always ask a grown-up before you share anything.

blocks.alt: A phone that listens to your voice uses AI to understand the words.
blocks.caption: A phone that listens to your voice uses AI to understand the words.

question.prompt: It is safe to tell strangers online your password.

blocks.prompt: Can you think of a machine at home that follows instructions?
blocks.answer_markdown: A washing machine, a microwave, a TV remote or a toy robot all follow instructions.

blocks.title: Computer pairs
blocks.goal: Turn over two cards and find the pairs.

points: Computers follow instructions in order. A list of steps is an algorithm.
We can sort things and spot patterns.
Data can be shown with tally marks and pictograms.
A bug is a mistake. Debugging fixes it.
AI learns from examples, and we keep our password secret.

blocks.markdown: When you are ready, start the quiz. It has 15 questions and takes about 15 minutes. Do your best!

What comes first, next and last.
Things that repeat in the same order.
To put things into groups that go together.
Information we collect, like how many children like apples.
A graph that uses pictures to show how many.
How we tell a computer something, like a keyboard.
How a computer tells us something, like a screen.
A mistake in a set of instructions.
Short for artificial intelligence. A computer that learns from examples.
A computer program that learns from lots of examples to do a job.
A secret word that keeps your accounts safe. Never share it.
